Sample
The sample comprised 299 Indian employees, most of whom
were full-time (81.3%), with an average firm tenure of 2.10 years
(range of .5 to 5 years). A majority of the participants were male
(59.5%), with a mean age of 26.18 (ranging from18 to 37). The
sampled employees were members of 71 teams with three to eight
employees per team (mean of 4.21 members). Each team served a
single client and performed sales or information technology func-
tions.

method, we conducted a cusp analysis to verify the use of cohort birth-
year cutoﬀs (i.e., 1978 and 1990). The cusp of each generation (i.e.,
participants born in the last ﬁve years of each period) and the core
generation (i.e., the other participants born in the period) were em-
pirically compared. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) post hoc group
comparisons revealed no signiﬁcant diﬀerences between the core pre-
reform (born 1961–1972) and cusp pre-reform generations (born
1973–1977). Participants born in the cusp pre-reform generation dif-
fered in openness-to-change values (mean diﬀerence [m.d.] = 0.10,
p = 0.002) and conservation values (m.d. = 0.10, p = 0.018) from
those born in the core reform generation (1978–1984). The core reform
and cusp reform generations (born 1985–1989) had similar value or-
ientations, and members of the cusp reform and post-reform genera-
tions (1990–1998) had value diﬀerences (self-transcendence values,
